documents.title: INTIMATION FOR RESCHEDULING OF 60TH ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE COMPANY ON 26TH AUGUST 2026 (WEDNESDAY) AT 12:00 NOON (IST)

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported its Q4 FY26 and full year results, achieving a highest-ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT and strong physical performance despite operational challenges and shutdowns. Management highlighted successful execution of energy efficiency measures, record distillate yields, and comfortable debt-equity levels alongside increased dividend payouts. The company is advancing key capex projects, including Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS and retail outlets, while navigating geopolitical and crude price volatility through flexible crude sourcing. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited reported its financial and operational performance for Q4 FY25, highlighting resilient crude throughput and efficiency gains despite lower international product cracks compared to the previous year. Management discussed capital expenditure plans, including maintenance outlays and the proposed LOBS project, alongside updates on the Cauvery basin refinery joint venture.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted that Motor Spirit (MS) in the southern market faces a clear shortfall where production is less than demand.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has all approvals in place for the Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project, and execution has started in full swing.
capex_expansion.quote: Some of the important projects that we'll be taking up is Group 2, Group 3 LOBS for which all approvals are in place and the project execution has started in full swing.

capex_expansion.claim: The retail outlet endeavor for which 300 licenses were taken has started, and FY27 will see a lot of commissioning out of them.
capex_expansion.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

capex_expansion.claim: The Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project is budgeted at INR 1,600 crores and the retail outlet project at INR 400 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: Normal maintenance capex is estimated at around INR 500 crores every year.
capex_expansion.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

capex_expansion.claim: The company reported capital expenditure of Rs. 673 crores for the current year.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: Management stated that the revised capital cost for the CBR project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

margins_costs.claim: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: Foreign exchange losses for the quarter were approximately INR 200 crores, and for the full year around INR 350 crores.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: The full year GRM for 2024-25 stood at $4.22 per barrel compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: The fuel and loss for the year as a whole came down to 8.51%.
margins_costs.quote: I must place it that if you remember our Energy Indexes and our Fuel and Loss Indexes were quite high 2-3 years back and we went to a roadmap where we said on a sustained basis, we will bring it down to very efficient levels and in that context, the fuel and loss has come down to 8.51% for the year as a whole.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, which is equivalent to 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: In quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.93 MMT, representing 111% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The new Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS unit will add a fresh capacity of 250 KTPA.
orders_capacity.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of installed capacity during the year.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year and if you take that into consideration , you will find that this performance is quite comparable to the previous year's performance where CPCL clocked 111% capacity utilization and coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

capital_allocation.claim: The debt-equity ratio stands at 0.18 on a gross level compared to 0.39 last year.
capital_allocation.quote: Our leverage position now stands at 0.18. Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: Gross borrowings are INR 1,900 crores and net borrowings are INR 973 crores, resulting in a net debt ratio of 0.09.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores. If we consider net borrowing, the debt ratio is only 0.09, which is less than 0.1.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a final dividend of INR 54 per share, which, combined with the interim dividend of INR 8, brings the total dividend to INR 62 per share.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: The debt-to-equity position as on March 31, 2025, stands at 0.39 with absolute debt at Rs. 3,100 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year. At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to logistical constraints and volatility of crude oil prices pose challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management noted that uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices pose a challenge.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

management_commitments.claim: The INR 2,000 crores total capex for the LOBS and retail outlet projects will happen over 2 to 3 years.
management_commitments.quote: This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: Management stated that the normal maintenance capital expenditure for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
